evidence: Read cold in 'Before you begin', the 'Deciding to do it' paragraph. DRAFT: 'Remind yourself that if you say 'stop' at any time, the induction will end. If you say 'less', you will be asked to do less. If you say 'quiet', the talking will stop.' CHANGE CHECK: it replaces the two sentences in SOURCE.txt (Know that you can say stop at any time and the induction will end; if you want to change something, say less ... or say quiet and the talking will stop) with three stop lines, one per control word, in the order stop, less, quiet, which is the order of SOURCE.txt's card. It does what the_change says. MEANING: the card says 'Stop' ends the exercise, 'less' reduces the demand, 'quiet' stops the words. The draft says stop ends the induction, less means being asked to do less, quiet stops the talking. Same three effects, and nothing added: no claim about a study, person, product or Joel's life (C03, C04 absent). The card's other two points (open your eyes and finish; no inner part has to approve the decision to stop) are carried by the paragraph's own next two sentences, which this change does not touch, and which pick up from the draft well: 'You can also just open your eyes and stop' reads as a second way to stop after the three words. Small shifts, none a fail: 'Know that you can say stop' becomes 'Remind yourself that if you say stop' (an assurance becomes a rehearsal, no new fact); the replaced words' framing 'If you want to change something' is gone, but each line says what its word does, which is the point; 'asking for less from you' becomes 'asked to do less', which is the same reduced demand. FLOW AND REFERENTS: it follows 'If you are going to use a recording, read the script if you can' naturally (plan, preview, read the script, remind yourself of the exits). 'the induction' is anchored earlier on the page ('what you want to do during the induction'); 'the talking' is whoever is speaking, which the recording and script named just before it, and the narrator named in the next paragraph, make clear; the passive 'you will be asked' has the induction as its obvious agent. 'Remind yourself' presupposes the reader may already know the stop words although this is their first mention on the page, but that is ordinary self-help usage and not a stumble. No unclear pronoun (C02) and no 'the kid' (C01). TELL ROWS: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the literal draft in its context. One row is actually happening, in a mild way: T02. Three consecutive compressed 'if you say X, Y' conditions each do one clean job and hand off to the next, inside a paragraph that is itself a run of short questions and commands. I judge it justified. The three lines are three different real controls in the order of his published list (a list alone is not the tell), the card's own line is the same three-part parallel, the parallel form is what makes a safety list findable and rememberable, and the paragraph breaks out of the run afterwards with an afterthought ('You can also just open your eyes and stop, and then come all the way back anyway') and an aside ('even if a part tells you that you do'). The writer's ledger says T02 ABSENT ('not part of a run of compressed commands'); I read the paragraph as a checklist run, so I record it here instead. Other close calls, judged absent: T12 and T09 (three equal-weight lines, but the three words are the actual controls and not a symmetry made for balance); T13 (the lines only fill slots, but the paragraph around them carries asides and counter-considerations); T22 ('Remind yourself' sounds coach-like, but the sentence carries a rule, what each word does, so it is not reassurance alone); T20 and T29 ('the talking will stop' is a short line, but the paragraph goes on for two more sentences, so it is not a closer); T26 ('stop' recurs as control word and as verb, but stopping is the paragraph's subject, and 'less ... do less' glosses the word at no cost); T15 (the frame is changed from two sentences to three, so this is not word-swapping inside the old structure). LINTER FINDINGS: (a) 'B7 short landing at paragraph end', flagged on 'If you say 'quiet', the talking will stop.': the linter saw the draft alone; in the article the paragraph continues with two more sentences after it, so it is not the landing. Accepted. (The writer's reason also cites 'Don’t fake it.', which belongs to a different change; I rely only on the in-context fact.) (b) 'D9 follows the source order', 1 of 1 paragraphs: the order stop, less, quiet is the card's own order and nothing else would read better; each line states a distinct effect. Accepted. (c) 'E36/E41 heavy second person', 12.1 per 100 words (4 'you' in 33): the 'you' here is the one who says the word, the actor of each rule, not reassurance padding, and the whole page speaks to 'you'. Accepted. (d) the O30 repeated-phrase finding, the phrase 'you say' three times: the repeat is three parallel rules, each naming a different word and its effect, which is the instruction itself; the replaced words also said 'say' three times, so this is not a new repeat; and unlike Joel's 'as adults' case, no repeated word is a redundant extra, since each sentence adds a different control. Accepted, with the note that he may prefer the shorter published form of the card ('Stop' ends it; 'less' asks less; 'quiet' stops the words) if the triple 'If you say' feels heavy to him; that is his call and not a defect in the change. Verdict PASS: it does what the_change says, keeps the source meaning, adds nothing, has no unjustified tell, and reads right where it sits.
